_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Tunisia covering Capsian culture, Phoenician Carthage, Punic Wars, Roman Africa (El Djem, Dougga), early Christianity (Tertullian, St Augustine nearby), Vandal and Byzantine rule, Arab conquest, Aghlabid and Hafsid dynasties, Ottoman regency, French protectorate 1881, Bourguiba modernisation, Ben Ali police state, 2010-2011 Jasmine Revolution (Arab Spring origin), and democratic transition challenges.

religion.note: Djerba synagogue (El Ghriba) is one of oldest in Africa; Jewish community ~1,000 remaining

ethnic_groups.name: Arab
ethnic_groups.notes: Arabic-speaking majority; heavily arabised Berber heritage; tribal identities less prominent than in Libya

ethnic_groups.name: Arabised Berber
ethnic_groups.notes: Historically Berber/Amazigh but culturally/linguistically arabised; many Tunisians of mixed ancestry; Berber identity reviving

ethnic_groups.name: Berber (Amazigh)
ethnic_groups.notes: Small communities in Djerba, Matmata, Douiret, Chenini; Shelha language speakers; troglodyte villages

ethnic_groups.name: Black Tunisian
ethnic_groups.notes: Sub-Saharan descent; legacy of trans-Saharan slave trade; southern regions; discrimination issues; 2018 anti-racism law

ethnic_groups.name: European/Other
ethnic_groups.notes: Small French, Italian, Maltese communities; most Europeans left after independence; Turkish descent from Ottoman era

country_profile.notes_unique: Site of ancient Carthage, Rome's greatest rival; birthplace of the 2011 Arab Spring (Jasmine Revolution); the Saharan oasis town of Tozeur was a Star Wars filming location.

natural_resources.notes: World's 5th-largest phosphate producer (Gafsa basin, CPG); oil production declining (~35,000 bpd); dates (Deglet Nour, world-class quality); olive oil (2nd/3rd largest global exporter); fisheries; significant solar energy potential (Saharan south).

military.notes: Professional apolitical military (did not fire on protesters during 2011 revolution); counter-terrorism operations (Chaambi Mountains, Libyan border); USAFRICOM Major Non-NATO Ally; deployed buffer zone border with Libya; arms from US, France, Turkey.

infrastructure.notes: Ooredoo, Tunisie Telecom, Orange telecoms; good digital infrastructure; fibre expansion; TGM light metro.

debt_aid.notes: Birthplace of Arab Spring (2010-11); economy struggled post-revolution; President Saied's 2021 power consolidation; IMF $1.9B deal stalled; subsidy reform resistance; EU migration cooperation deal; Tunisian dinar closely managed; Carthage historical tourism asset.

education.notes: High tertiary enrollment for Africa/MENA; Bourguiba-era education investment; French-Arabic bilingual system; high graduate unemployment (~30%); strong STEM tradition; engineering schools prestigious; PISA participation but low scores.

diaspora_migration.diaspora_population: 1.5 million+ (France, Italy, Germany, Gulf states, Canada, Libya)
diaspora_migration.notes: Remittances significant (~5.5% GDP); large French-Tunisian community; irregular migration surge to Italy via boats (Sfax/Lampedusa route); sub-Saharan migrants transit through Tunisia; post-revolution youth 'harragas' (irregular migrants).
diaspora_migration.immigration_policy: Transit country for sub-Saharan migration to Europe; 2023 anti-migrant incidents

digital_economy.notes: Elgazala Technopark (2001, first in Africa); strong nearshoring/BPO for French market; Startup Act 2018 (progressive startup legislation); Tunisie Telecom, Ooredoo, Orange operators; submarine cables to Europe; 50,000+ IT professionals; francophone tech outsourcing hub.

geography.terrain: Atlas Mountains (north); fertile Tell region; central steppes; Saharan south (Grand Erg Oriental); salt lakes (chotts); Mediterranean coastline
geography.notes: Northernmost point of Africa (Cap Angela/Ras ben Sakka); Carthage (ancient Phoenician/Roman, UNESCO); Star Wars filming (Matmata, Tataouine); Arab Spring origin (2010-11).

economy_extended.notes: Economic challenges (post-revolution stagnation); phosphates/olive oil major exports; auto/aerospace manufacturing (nearshoring Europe); Kais Saied power consolidation; IMF loan negotiations; youth unemployment crisis.

health.notes: CNAM (social health insurance); strong public health system; medical brain drain (to France/Gulf); medical tourism (dental/cosmetic); NCD transition.

food_agriculture.notes: World's 2nd largest olive oil producer (after EU); Saharan date palms (Tozeur/Nefta deglet nour); wheat imports critical; fishing (tuna, octopus); water scarcity challenge.

energy.notes: STEG utility; declining oil/gas production; solar potential enormous (Sahara); TuNur CSP export project (to Europe via Italy); Borj Cédria solar research.

transport.notes: SNCFT railway (north/south); Tunis light rail (TGM line, oldest light metro in Africa); motorways expanding; multiple international airports (tourism).

major_attractions: Sidi Bou Said (blue and white village)
tourism.notes: 9 UNESCO sites; mass tourism (beach + cultural); Star Wars filming locations; Carthage/Roman heritage; recovering post-2015 Bardo/Sousse attacks; Djerba (2023 UNESCO).

human_rights_gender.notes: Most progressive women's rights in Arab world (Code of Personal Status 1956, Bourguiba); democratic backsliding under Kais Saied (2021 power grab); anti-Black African migrant rhetoric (2023); Article 230 (homosexuality).

security_stability.notes: Post-2015 attacks (Bardo/Sousse terrorism), improved security; Libya border concern; democratic backsliding under Saied; migration crisis (sub-Saharan transit to Europe); border wall with Libya.

cultural_heritage.film_industry: Notable (Carthage Film Festival (JCC), oldest African film festival; Abdellatif Kechiche director)
notable_historical_figures: Habib Bourguiba (Father of the Nation, 1st president)
Tahar Ben Jelloun (novelist, shared with Morocco)
cultural_heritage.media_landscape: Wataniya TV state; Nessma, Attessia (private); post-revolution media pluralism diminishing under Saied; TAP (state news agency)
cultural_heritage.notes: Jasmine Revolution (2010-11, Arab Spring origin); Carthage heritage; harissa UNESCO; 1956 Code of Personal Status (women's rights pioneer); Mediterranean-Berber-Arab identity.

legal_system.legal_tradition: Civil law (French system) with Islamic law influences
legal_system.sharia_applicability: Personal status influenced by Islamic principles (reformed by Bourguiba 1956); 2022 constitution references Islam as state religion
legal_system.notes: 2022 constitution replaced 2014 (Kais Saied; concentrates presidential power); Code of Personal Status (most progressive in Arab world); Cour de Cassation.

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global.
comparative_rankings.notes: #3 HDI in Africa; Arab Spring birthplace; manufacturing nearshoring hub.

current_leader.name: Kais Saied
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: Independent/populist; constitutional law professor; suspended parliament July 2021; new constitution 2022 concentrating power in presidency; critics call it a coup; crackdown on opposition and migrants

former_leaders.name: Habib Bourguiba
former_leaders.notes: Father of independence; Supreme Combatant; modernised Tunisia: women's rights (Personal Status Code 1956), secularism, education; president-for-life; removed by Ben Ali in 'medical coup'

former_leaders.name: Zine El Abidine Ben Ali
former_leaders.notes: Police state; RCD party; economic growth but severe corruption; wife Leila Trabelsi/clan; fled to Saudi Arabia January 14, 2011 (Jasmine Revolution); died in exile 2019

former_leaders.name: Beji Caid Essebsi
former_leaders.notes: Nidaa Tounes; oldest elected head of state in Africa at 88; died in office July 2019; veteran Bourguibist
